result.topic_en: Conclusion of Euler's treatment of an elastic lamina fixed by a stylus at its midpoint: two cases yield frequency equations, which are identified with the principal vibration case and Problem II for a lamina of half length, with a remark on extending the method to several fixed points.
result.transcription:
LAMINARVM ELASTICARVM. 487
et ſi loco V eius valor ſubſtituatur, reperietur
$2 = -\cos .\zeta\,(e^{\zeta} + e^{-\zeta})$
II. Sin autem ſumamus $D' = D$ debebit eſſe
$(V+1)\cos \zeta + (V-1)\sin .\zeta - V e^{\zeta} - e^{-\zeta} = 0,$
ex quo pro V ſubſtituto valore habebitur
$e^{2\zeta} = \frac{\cos .\zeta + \sin .\zeta}{\cos .\zeta - \sin .\zeta}.$
Vnde patet priori caſu laminam perinde contremiſcere, atque in noſtra euolutione principali, ſi longitudo laminae tantum ad ſemiſſin reduceretur, poſteriori vero caſu tremores conuenient cum Problemate ſecundo, ſi ibi etiam longitudo laminae duplo ſumatur minor, ſiue aequalis ſemiſſi noſtrae laminae A B. Atque hinc facile intelligere licet, quomodo calculus inſtitui deberet, ſi lamina adeo in pluribus punctis ſtylo figeretur.

DE

items.quote: Vnde patet priori caſu laminam perinde contremiſcere, atque in noſtra euolutione principali, ſi longitudo laminae tantum ad ſemiſſin reduceretur
items.english: Hence it is clear that in the first case the lamina vibrates just as in our principal development, if only the length of the lamina were reduced to half.

items.quote: poſteriori vero caſu tremores conuenient cum Problemate ſecundo, ſi ibi etiam longitudo laminae duplo ſumatur minor, ſiue aequalis ſemiſſi noſtrae laminae A B
items.english: In the latter case, however, the vibrations will agree with Problem II, if there too the length of the lamina is taken half as large, i.e. equal to half of our lamina AB.

items.quote: Atque hinc facile intelligere licet, quomodo calculus inſtitui deberet, ſi lamina adeo in pluribus punctis ſtylo figeretur.
items.english: And from this it is easy to understand how the calculation should be set up if the lamina were fixed by a stylus at several points.
